messages.subject: bar chart and faceting question
parts:
Hello,

First of all, wish you all Merry Christmas and happy new year :)

I have the data shown below and I would like to plot it as a bar chart where the x axis shows every distinct combination of levels for the two factors No_middleware and No_databases and the y axis (the bar) shows the Demand (Dmw and Ddb) for each of the factors (two bars in dodge position).

My x axis ideally would look like (No_middleware,No_databases) with all combinations of the two factors 3x2=6:

(1,1) (1,4) (2,1) (2,4) (4,1) (4,4)

My y axis bars are gonna be the respective demand values for each i.e. Dmw and Ddb.

And then finally these two "faceted" by the Partitioning factor.

Usually I look for similar use cases in internet and quickly find them, I also try to find a quick solution in the ggplot2 book but in this case even though the use-case is not too complicated it seems daunting to get using ggplot2. Can anyone advice?

Many thanks in advance,
Best regards,
Giovanni

messages.subject: Re: bar chart and faceting question
parts:
Hi,

Once you learn ggplot2, you will find that ggplot2 is very useful and
excellent tool for this type of visualization.
Here is an example:

> head(df)

26 sharding 1 1 18771.96 3921.148
28 sharding 1 4 17825.57 2971.827
30 replication 1 1 18448.43 4562.610
32 replication 1 4 16900.78 8744.177
34 sharding 2 1 56256.48 3751.755
36 sharding 2 4 16256.61 5115.520
>
> df2 <- melt(df, id = 1:3)
> df2$x <- paste(df2$No_mid, df2$No_dat, sep = "_")
> head(df2)
Partitioning No_middleware No_databases variable value
1 sharding 1 1 Dmw 18771.96
2 sharding 1 4 Dmw 17825.57
3 replication 1 1 Dmw 18448.43
4 replication 1 4 Dmw 16900.78
5 sharding 2 1 Dmw 56256.48
6 sharding 2 4 Dmw 16256.61
x
1 1_1
2 1_4
3 1_1
4 1_4
5 2_1
6 2_4
>
> ggplot(df2, aes(x, value, fill = variable)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") + facet_wrap(~Partitioning)

messages.subject: Re: bar chart and faceting question
parts:
Hi Kohske,

Thank you so much for your help. Your example was very enlightening and helped me figure out what I needed to do. I realized my problem was the way the data was layout, so I fixed it. I include my final solution below.

The final ggplot2 call I to get what I needed was:

ggplot(df,aes(x, value, fill=Device)) + opts(title='Demand per Device for the 2^k factorial simulation') +  
xlab('Number of (Middleware, Databases)') + ylab('Demand (ms)') +
geom_bar(stat="identity",position="dodge") +
facet_wrap(~Partitioning)

Thank you again!
Best regards,
Giovanni
